Methodology — what these numbers mean

Value factor — the farm's average selling price compared with the average price in its region over the same period (industry shorthand: generation-weighted price ÷ time-weighted price, VWAP ÷ TWAP). Above 100% means the farm's energy is worth more than the average MWh. Solar sliding below 100% is the well-known midday "cannibalisation" effect; wind that blows into the evening peak can exceed 100%.

Capacity factor — average output as a share of maximum (nameplate) capacity. Capacities marked ~ are estimated from the unit's own observed output (99.7th percentile) because it isn't in the hand-checked registry — treat those as indicative.

Output at negative prices — the share of the farm's generation produced while its regional spot price was below $0. Revenue counts wholesale energy sales only: no contracts (PPAs), green certificates (LGCs), or system-services (FCAS) income.

Fine print: the regional average price is the full-month average even when a farm ran for only part of the month — a farm commissioned mid-month is compared against the whole month's market. Revenue covers intervals where both output and price data are present. Source: AEMO NEMweb dispatch SCADA (as-generated MW, not settlement metering) and dispatch prices. Registry names and capacities are approximate public data.
